premises.text: Passwords fail because human forgetfulness and negligence cause most breaches, and existing SSO/IAM/password managers are hard to adopt and centralize secrets in the cloud
premises.evidence_span: over 86% of breaches today are caused by users and not by hackers

premises.text: Phone-authenticated MyKey pushes credentials and 2FA tokens to the browser and can remotely disconnect sessions without teaching users a new login paradigm
premises.evidence_span: push her username, her password, and even the additional SMS token for two-factor authentication, directly from her phone to her browser

premises.text: Admins get real-time visibility to share, grant, revoke, privilege-limit, and geo/time/IP-rule access, plus background and scheduled password changes, without service-provider integrations
premises.evidence_span: It is a single ecosystem for sharing, revoking, and granting access

premises.text: Initial GTM targets medium-sized companies of 10–50 users, with freemium pricing before expanding upmarket
premises.evidence_span: initially targeting medium-sized companies that have between 10 and 50 users

value.text: Teams manage digital workspace access simply and securely without complicated, expensive tools
value.evidence_span: fundamentally changing the way teams manage access to the digital workspace

causal_links.evidence_span: we've seen how Myki makes it easy for the user to log in
MyKey is free for the first five users and then starts at $5, $4.99 per additional user per month

notes: User-caused breaches, hard-to-adopt tools, and cloud single-point-of-failure folded as one password-problem bundle (v1.5.1 §4.1.6). Admin features (revoke, privileges, geo/time/IP rules, password rotate, group provision) folded as cascade of one admin-control mechanism (§4.1.7); no-integration claim kept inside that module. Early-customer traction excluded. Price with segment targeting as one commercial/GTM premise. Anti-template: problem, product, and GTM separately revisable.
